extracted.intended_audience: newspaper readers and labor-management stakeholders (union officials, corporate negotiators, policymakers)
extracted.subtask_description: A news report summarizing management and union demands/proposals for terms to be included in new collective bargaining agreements (GM, Ford, UAW and others), plus related procedural/authority issues raised before governmental fact-finding boards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreement contains only collectively bargained provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: This agreement shall contain only such provisions as are collectively bargained and actually agreed to by the parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GM stated readiness to negotiate an agreement covering wages, hours and conditions of employment but insisted the written contract include only matters formally bargained and agreed to.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pattern of past contractual relationships (national + local supplements)
rubrics_metrics.description: The pattern of past contractual relationships, namely a national agreement covering appropriate matters common to similar or related bargaining units and supplemental local agreements authorized by such national agreement, be followed in negotiations between the parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GM proposed using prior national/local agreement structure as the basis for new negotiations and offered to review which bargaining units should be included in a new national agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subjects limited to wages, hours and conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: That wages, hours of employment and other conditions of employment are the only matters which are subject to collective bargaining.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Management demanded that collective bargaining be confined to traditional labor subjects and excluded matters such as production, plant location, methods, and other managerial prerogatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee freedom and restrictions on solicitation/dues
rubrics_metrics.description: That the union and the corporation shall recognize the rights of employees and applicants for employment to elect or refuse membership in any union, to maintain or resign from such membership, to enjoy freedom from restraint and discrimination, coercion with respect to work, employment, union membership and union activity. Solicitation for union membership and collection of dues shall not take place during working hours, on company time or at company expense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Management sought explicit protections for employees' free choice regarding union membership and limits on union solicitation/dues collection during company time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management rights (products, plant location, production schedules, methods, hiring/firing/discipline)
rubrics_metrics.description: That the products to be manufactured, the location of plants, the schedules of production, the methods, processes and means of manufacturing, the right to hire, promote, transfer, discharge or discipline for cause, and to maintain discipline and efficiency of employees, are the sole responsibility of the corporation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A broad 'management rights' clause requested by GM to reserve operational control entirely to management and exclude these matters from collective bargaining.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance procedure patterned on prior agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: That grievances of employees, defined as alleged specific violations of a provision of the national agreement or local agreements, be handled in accordance with a grievance procedure patterned after that provided for in prior collective bargaining agreements, with such modifications as are necessary to simplify and expedite the disposition of grievances and to eliminate the abuses which developed under prior grievance procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GM asked that the grievance machinery be retained but reformed to be faster and less abuse-prone; most other demands amplified existing contract grievance and bargaining-process provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seniority accrual and probationary period
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to appropriate rules, definitions and procedures with respect to transfer, loss of seniority and lay-off, employees other than veterans of World War II shall acquire seniority after a probationary period of twelve consecutive months during which they shall acquire no rights with respect to re-employment if laid off or discharged during such period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Management proposed a 12-month probationary window before seniority rights vest for non-veteran hires, limiting re-employment rights during that time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment for committeemen time (split cost)
rubrics_metrics.description: That the wages to be paid to union committeemen for time spent off their jobs in handling grievances or negotiating with the management be paid one-half by the union and one-half by General Motors; and employment of committeemen on jobs other than their own only to the extent necessary to accomplish proper representation of the union.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GM sought cost-sharing for paid union representative time and limits on committee members' job reassignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leave of absence procedure reforms
rubrics_metrics.description: That there be a leave of absence procedure which eliminates the abuses which existed under the prior agreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Management requested a clear, abuse-resistant leave policy to replace problematic prior practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Union withdrawal of objection to incentive pay plans
rubrics_metrics.description: That the international union will withdraw objection to the local unions negotiating and agreeing to pay-plans which provide for rewarding individuals for increased productive effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GM asked the union to accept incentive (individual reward) pay-plans at local level; the corporation said the union previously objected to such plans (incentive wage plan).

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal employment opportunity for World War II veterans
rubrics_metrics.description: That there be equal employment opportunity for World War II veterans as compared to civilians hired during the war, irrespective of seniority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Management proposed giving veterans equal employment consideration regardless of seniority differences created by wartime hiring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum hiring wage and advancement timetable
rubrics_metrics.description: General Motors proposes that the minimum hiring wage rate for male and female employees in any General Motors plant be increased to 80 cents per hour; new employees hired at this minimum rate will be advanced to a job rate of 90 cents per hour in not more than six months' time in accordance with procedures to be negotiated locally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GM suggested raising the minimum hiring wage (above federal minimum) and a schedule for advancement to job rate within six months subject to local negotiation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalties for unauthorized work stoppages
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriate penalties, including loss of seniority, against any employee taking part in any strike or work stoppage in violation of the agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Management demanded disciplinary/financial penalties for illegal stoppages; Ford proposed a $5-a-day fine; union countered with a $3 first-offense/$5 subsequent fine deductible from pay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guarantee against union vilification/publications responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: An adequate guarantee that the union will make good on its pledge to eliminate personal attacks, false accusations and vilification of management through union publications, handbills, literature and releases; and that the international union as bargaining agent shall accept full responsibility for all items pertaining to management in such publications and releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GM sought an explicit commitment and liability from the international union to curb defamatory union publications and accept responsibility for management-related content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper representation in each bargaining unit (regulate to eliminate abuses)
rubrics_metrics.description: That the union be properly represented in each bargaining unit subject to appropriate conditions to reasonably regulate such representation, to eliminate abuses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Management requested rules around union representation at unit level to prevent representation abuses and to define committee pay and duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review and determination of bargaining unit coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: We are prepared to review the bargaining units which were covered in previous agreements to determine whether all such bargaining units should be included in the new national agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GM offered to reassess which units are included under a national pattern agreement as part of negotiations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance definition tied to specific contract provision violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievances of employees are to be defined as alleged specific violations of a provision of the national agreement or local agreements authorized and executed as supplements to the national agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GM emphasized narrowing grievance scope to concrete alleged contractual breaches, as opposed to broader or vague complaints.
